headline: Simulations tie proton transport and hydration in complex I to disease mutations
label: Physics Based Proton Transport Modeling
summary: Atomistic and multiscale reactive simulations now resolve how hydration and quinone binding govern Complex I proton transport.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of physics-based simulation to connect proton transport geometry and hydration to disease-relevant outcomes. Two Complex I preprints apply this approach directly. Atomistic molecular dynamics of human complex I indicate that the ND6 m.14484T>C mutation linked to Leber hereditary optic neuropathy disrupts quinone binding and hydration networks. A separate multiscale reactive molecular dynamics study uses a water wire connectivity metric to simulate proton transport along Complex I's lateral pathway, tying transport to hydration. The RPE65 preprint is methodologically distinct: it combines AlphaFold with variational quantum eigensolver simulation to propose an RQAS score relating proton-tunneling geometry to clinical severity in Leber congenital amaurosis. What is new across the set is the explicit treatment of hydration connectivity and proton tunneling as quantitative determinants of pathogenic severity, though the RPE65 link remains a proposed score rather than an established correlation.
